Package org.openxava.spring

Class OpenXavaAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.openxava.spring.OpenXavaAutoConfiguration
All Implemented Interfaces:
org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.WebMvcConfigurer
@AutoConfiguration @ConditionalOnClass({org.apache.catalina.startup.Tomcat.class,org.springframework.boot.tomcat.servlet.TomcatServletWebServerFactory.class}) @EnableConfigurationProperties(OpenXavaDataSourcesProperties.class) @ServletComponentScan(basePackages={"org.openxava","com.openxava"}) public class OpenXavaAutoConfiguration extends Object implements org.springframework.web.servlet.config.annotation.WebMvcConfigurer
Spring Boot auto-configuration for OpenXava.

Registers servlet components (via @ServletComponentScan), the default view controller for the root path, the WebSocket endpoint for chat, and if a Spring-managed DataSource is present, registers it in the Tomcat naming context under the JNDI name specified in persistence.xml, regardless of whether Tomcat is embedded (running with spring-boot:run or the main class) or external (the app deployed as a WAR on a standalone Tomcat). This ensures that both JPA/Hibernate and OpenXava JDBC utilities can resolve it, with the datasource configuration declared only once, in application.properties.

It also creates and registers any additional datasource declared in application.properties with the openxava.datasources.* prefix (see OpenXavaDataSourcesProperties), binding each one to its JNDI name so secondary persistence units can resolve them too.

Since:
8.0
Author:
Javier Paniza

    • openXavaTomcatCustomizer

      @Bean public org.springframework.boot.web.server.WebServerFactoryCustomizer<org.springframework.boot.tomcat.servlet.TomcatServletWebServerFactory> openXavaTomcatCustomizer(OpenXavaDataSourcesProperties dataSourcesProperties, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<DataSource> dataSourceProvider)
      Prepares the embedded Tomcat container so that JNDI resources can be registered, and registers the datasources in the Tomcat naming context during context customization (before filter initialization). This is critical for embedded Tomcat, where filters (e.g. NaviOXFilter) may trigger JPA/Hibernate initialization during their init() method, before ContextRefreshedEvent fires.

      For external Tomcat (WAR deployment), where context customizers do not run, the datasource registration is done by openXavaJndiRegistrar(org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<javax.sql.DataSource>, org.openxava.spring.OpenXavaDataSourcesProperties, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<jakarta.servlet.ServletContext>) on ContextRefreshedEvent.

      Since:
      8.0

    • openXavaJndiRegistrar

      @Bean public org.springframework.context.ApplicationListener<org.springframework.context.event.ContextRefreshedEvent> openXavaJndiRegistrar(org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<DataSource> dataSourceProvider, OpenXavaDataSourcesProperties dataSourcesProperties, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<jakarta.servlet.ServletContext> servletContextProvider)
      Creates the Spring-managed datasources declared for JNDI (the default one plus any declared with the openxava.datasources.* prefix) and registers them in the Tomcat naming context, both when Tomcat is embedded and when the application is deployed as a WAR on an external Tomcat. This way the datasource configuration only needs to be declared once, in application.properties.
      Since:
      8.0
